data.reasoning: Two models (deepseek-v4-flash and openrouter/free) independently reviewed both PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO and found no security issues. The PKGBUILD is a standard Go package build script with a pinned GitHub tarball source and valid SHA256 checksum. The .SRCINFO contains only metadata with no executable code. The qwen3-235b 'inconclusive' result was caused by an API error (HTTP 400) when reviewing .SRCINFO, not by any security concern. No malicious patterns, obfuscated code, or suspicious network operations were detected in any reviewed file.
data.disagreement_analysis: The apparent disagreement stems from a tool error in qwen3-235b (LLM API request failed with HTTP 400 BadRequestError when reviewing .SRCINFO), not from a security finding. This caused the overall result to be marked 'inconclusive' despite the PKGBUILD being marked safe. The other two models successfully reviewed both files and found no issues.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b failed to review .SRCINFO due to API error (HTTP 400), resulting in incomplete coverage
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, timeouts) should be clearly distinguished from security findings in the final verdict - an API error on one file should not cause the entire package to be marked 'inconclusive' when other files are successfully reviewed and found safe
The audit tool should implement retry logic or fallback mechanisms for transient API errors to prevent incomplete coverage from affecting verdicts
When multiple models agree on 'safe' and the only disagreement is due to tool errors rather than security findings, the consensus should be trusted
